2023.date_rule: start_date <= boundary and (end_date blank or end_date > boundary); account active if any linked subscription is active

2024.date_rule: start_date <= boundary and (end_date blank or end_date > boundary); account active if any linked subscription is active

cohorts.definition: Earliest positive-length subscription start month; active if any linked subscription is open under source date rule at the next month boundary.
cohorts.limitation: End dates, missing end dates, and event labels conflict; this is a conditional date-state matrix and must not be interpreted as verified customer retention.

metadata.source_window: 2023-01-01 through 2025-01-01 date boundary; source rows end 2024-12-31

methodology: Customer = distinct account_id, with simultaneous subscription rows collapsed to one account.
Opening active status is any subscription row satisfying start_date <= boundary and (end_date blank or end_date > boundary).
An account-date coverage gap is conditional on end_date being an effective end and no unrecorded subscription coverage.
Account churn flags are all-time labels; event rows are account-grain only and are not accepted as customer-loss outcomes when contradicted by active subscriptions.
The primary KPI remains UNKNOWN; conditional date calculations are disclosed separately.

primary_customer_churn.formula: Unique eligible customers lost during period / unique active customers at period start × 100
primary_customer_churn.reason: Subscription dates report no complete account-coverage losses for the 2024 opening base, while account-level departure events conflict with subscriptions still active on those dates; source semantics do not resolve the conflict.

movement_bridge.note: Boundary-set reconciliation under the subscription-date rule; not gross within-period customer movements.

segments.label_note: Descriptive label prevalence only; not historical churn or predictive risk.
